relationships.rationale: Every new exchange being a managed API depends on those APIs carrying semantic versions with a documented deprecation lifecycle.
Managed APIs are managed precisely because they are exposed and governed through the API gateway.
A managed API contract must express domain concepts in shared language, not the producer's internal data structures.
This strategy is the direct mandate for defaulting to asynchronous, event-driven messaging over synchronous calls.
Publishing all material state changes as events requires consumers to handle duplicate delivery gracefully, since producers do not guarantee exactly-once.
This strategy is the direct mandate for authoring and reviewing API and event schemas before implementation begins.
Reviewing contracts before implementation is what prevents producer-internal models from leaking into the shared integration model.
This strategy is the direct mandate for all inter-zone traffic to be mediated through the managed gateway or broker.
Integrations designed for reuse with stable contracts depend on versioned interfaces with an explicit, managed deprecation path.
Reusable integration capabilities must expose shared-language contracts independent of any single producer's internal implementation.
